questions.question: Which title was given to Begum Akhtar?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Queen of Ghazals**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Begum Akhtar**, also known as **Akhtari Bai Faizabadi**, was one of the most renowned Indian singers of the 20th century.
 
• She earned the title "**Queen of Ghazals**" for her soulful and emotive renditions of **ghazals**, a poetic form of expression often exploring themes like love, pain, and loss.
 
• Begum Akhtar was instrumental in popularizing **ghazals** as a mainstream music genre in India.
 
• Her contribution to Indian classical music extended beyond ghazals, as she was also adept at singing **Thumris** and **Dadras**.
 
• She was honored with prestigious awards such as the **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award** and the **Padma Bhushan** for her remarkable contribution to Indian music.
 
• Begum Akhtar's music is known for its **deep emotional resonance** and her ability to bring out the nuances of the Urdu language through her singing.
 
• Her legacy continues to inspire artists and music enthusiasts, and she remains a towering figure in the world of classical and semi-classical Indian music.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Queen of Thumris**__

 __
 
• While Begum Akhtar sang **Thumris**, she is primarily associated with ghazals rather than being called the "Queen of Thumris."
 
• **Thumri** is a semi-classical Indian music form that emphasizes romantic and devotional themes and is closely associated with the Lucknow and Banaras gharanas.
 
 
 
• **Queen of Qawwalis**__
 __
 
• **Qawwalis** are devotional songs in the Sufi tradition and are not the genre for which Begum Akhtar is renowned.
 
• Qawwali is typically performed in groups, with singers like **Ustad Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan** being more synonymous with this genre.
 
 
 
• **Queen of Khayals**__
 
 
• **Khayal** is a form of Hindustani classical music that emphasizes improvisation and intricate melodies.
 
• Begum Akhtar did not focus on Khayal singing, as her fame primarily rested on ghazals, Thumris, and Dadras.

 __

questions.question: Rajashree Shirke was awarded Sangeet Natak Akademi for her contribution to which of the following dance forms?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Kathak**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rajashree Shirke**, a renowned Indian dancer, was awarded the **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award** for her contribution to the classical dance form of **Kathak**.
 
• **Kathak** is one of the eight major classical dance forms of India and has its origins in the **northern part of the country.**
 
• The word **"Kathak"** is derived from the Sanskrit word **"Katha,"** meaning "story," and the dance involves storytelling through intricate footwork, facial expressions, and graceful movements.
 
• Kathak was historically performed by **storytellers or bards** in temples to narrate mythological tales, primarily about **Lord Krishna, Lord Rama, and other Hindu deities.**
 
• The dance form evolved during the **Mughal period**, incorporating elements of Persian dance and music, which added a distinct flavor to Kathak.
 
• Kathak has three major **gharanas** (styles) - **Lucknow, Jaipur, and Banaras.**
 
• The dance form is characterized by intricate **footwork, spins (chakkars), rhythmic patterns (tihai), and expressive gestures (abhinaya).**
 
• The Sangeet Natak Akademi Award is a prestigious honor given by the **National Academy of Music, Dance, and Drama** in India to recognize artists' contributions to performing arts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Odissi**__

 __
 
• **Odissi** is a classical dance form that originated in the state of **Odisha**.
 
• It is known for its **graceful movements** and depiction of themes related to **Lord Jagannath** and Hindu mythology.
 
• Odissi incorporates elements such as **bhanga (body posture), mudras (hand gestures), and abhinaya** (expressive acting).
 
 
 
• **Kuchipudi**__
 __
 
• **Kuchipudi** is a classical dance form that originated in **Andhra Pradesh.**
 
• It is known for its **fluid movements, quick footwork, and dramatic storytelling.**
 
• Kuchipudi often combines **dance, music, and acting** to narrate mythological stories.
 
 
 
• **Manipuri**__
 
 
• **Manipuri** is a classical dance form that originates from the state of **Manipur.**
 
• This dance form is known for its **soft, graceful movements** and spiritual themes, often focusing on **Raslila** of Lord Krishna and Radha.

questions.question: Which ruler of Haryanka Dynasty annexed several important and powerful kingdoms in its vicinity such as Kosala, Kashi and Vajji?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Ajatashatru** was a ruler of the **Haryanka Dynasty**, which ruled over Magadha during the ancient period.
 
• He is known for his military campaigns and the annexation of several powerful kingdoms such as **Kosala, Kashi, and Vajji.**
 
• Ajatashatru is credited with initiating the expansion of **Magadha**, which later became a dominant kingdom in ancient India.
 
• He used advanced war technologies like **catapults and covered chariots** to strengthen his armies and subdue rival kingdoms.
 
• Ajatashatru’s conquest of **Vajji** was significant, as it involved defeating the republican confederacy led by the **Lichhavis**.
 
• He was instrumental in laying the foundation for the emergence of Magadha as a central power in the political landscape of ancient India.
 
• Ajatashatru played a crucial role in the promotion of **Buddhism**, as he was a contemporary of Lord Buddha and is said to have patronized the first Buddhist council.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Udayabhadra**__

 __
 
• **Udayabhadra** was the successor of Ajatashatru but is not prominently known for territorial expansion or military conquests.
 
• His reign is considered relatively peaceful compared to Ajatashatru’s aggressive expansion policies.
 
 
 
• **Nagadarshaka**__
 __
 
• **Nagadarshaka** was a ruler of the Haryanka Dynasty, but his contributions were not as significant in terms of military campaigns or territorial annexations.
 
• He is believed to have been overthrown, leading to the establishment of the **Shishunaga Dynasty.**
 
 
 
• **Shishunaga**__
 
 
• **Shishunaga** was the founder of the **Shishunaga Dynasty**, which succeeded the Haryanka Dynasty.
 
• He is known for consolidating power in Magadha after the decline of the Haryanka rulers.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution instructs the State to ensure a uniform civil code for all citizens?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Article 44**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 44** of the **Indian Constitution** falls under the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP).
 
• It directs the State to work towards ensuring a **Uniform Civil Code (UCC)** across the country for all its citizens.
 
• A **Uniform Civil Code** seeks to replace personal laws based on the scriptures and customs of each major religious community in India with a common set governing every citizen.
 
• The aim of Article 44 is to promote **national integration** and ensure equality and justice in society.
 
• The **UCC** is meant to address issues like marriage, divorce, inheritance, and adoption under a common framework.
 
• Although Article 44 is not enforceable by the courts (as it is part of the DPSP), it serves as a guiding principle for the **legislature and the government** in framing laws.
 
• The implementation of a Uniform Civil Code remains a subject of debate and discussion due to India's **diverse religious and cultural practices.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 46**__

 __
 
• **Article 46** of the Indian Constitution relates to the **promotion of the educational and economic interests** of Scheduled Castes (SC), Scheduled Tribes (ST), and other weaker sections of society.
 
• It directs the State to protect these groups from **social injustice** and all forms of exploitation.
 
 
 
• **Article 42**__
 __
 
• **Article 42** of the Indian Constitution pertains to the provision for **just and humane conditions of work** and maternity relief.
 
• It emphasizes the welfare of workers and the importance of creating a safe and equitable work environment.
 
 
 
• **Article 48**__
 
 
• **Article 48** of the Indian Constitution deals with the organization of agriculture and animal husbandry.
 
• It includes provisions for the **preservation and improvement of breeds** and the prohibition of slaughter of cows, calves, and other milch and draught cattle.

questions.question: The temperature does not fall beyond freezing point of water in the northern plains of India in winter because:

options.text: of the moderating influence of the sea
the Himalayas prevent the cold Siberian winds from entering India
it is far away from Jammu and Kashmir
of western disturbances during the cold winter season

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**The Himalayas prevent the cold Siberian winds from entering India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Himalayas** act as a natural barrier that prevents the entry of the cold **Siberian winds** from reaching the northern plains of India.
 
• The cold winds originate from the **Siberian region** of Russia, which experiences extremely low temperatures during winter.
 
• These winds are responsible for freezing conditions in parts of Central Asia. However, their impact is significantly reduced in India due to the presence of the Himalayas.
 
• The Himalayas block these winds and help maintain a relatively moderate winter climate in the northern plains of India.
 
• This natural barrier ensures that the temperature in the northern plains does not drop below the **freezing point of water**.
 
• The Himalayas also play a crucial role in influencing the overall climate of India, including the monsoons and seasonal variations.
 
• Without the Himalayas, the northern plains would experience much colder winters, similar to regions in Central Asia.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Moderating influence of the sea**__

 __
 
• The northern plains of India are located far away from the coastal regions, so the **influence of the sea** is minimal.
 
• Coastal areas experience more moderate temperatures due to the thermal properties of water, but this is not applicable to the northern plains.
 
 
 
• **Far away from Jammu and Kashmir**__
 __
 
• While Jammu and Kashmir do experience freezing temperatures, their geographical distance from the northern plains does not directly impact the winter conditions in the plains.
 
• The main factor here remains the presence of the Himalayas, not the proximity to Jammu and Kashmir.
 
 
 
• **Western disturbances during the cold winter season**__
 
 
• **Western disturbances** are extratropical storms originating in the Mediterranean region, which bring winter rainfall to northern India.
 
• These disturbances can cause temperature fluctuations but do not have a significant role in preventing temperatures from falling below freezing.

questions.question: Which Russian chemist's periodic table was published in a German magazine in 1872?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dmitri Mendeleev**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dmitri Mendeleev** was a renowned Russian chemist who is credited with the creation of the first widely accepted **Periodic Table of Elements**.
 
• His periodic table was published in a German magazine in the year **1872**. This made his work accessible to a global audience.
 
• Mendeleev organized the elements based on their **atomic weights** and properties, leading to the formulation of the **Periodic Law**, which states that the properties of elements are a periodic function of their atomic weights.
 
• One of Mendeleev's significant achievements was his ability to **predict the existence and properties of undiscovered elements**. For instance, he predicted elements such as **gallium, scandium, and germanium**, which were discovered later and fit perfectly into his table.
 
• His periodic table laid the foundation for the modern periodic table, which is now based on the **atomic number** instead of atomic weight.
 
• Mendeleev's work was pivotal in establishing the systematic study of chemistry and understanding the relationships between elements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Henry Moseley**__

 __
 
• **Henry Moseley** was a British physicist who made significant contributions to the understanding of the periodic table by introducing the concept of **atomic number**.
 
• He demonstrated that the periodic table should be arranged based on the **atomic number** rather than atomic weight, which resolved inconsistencies in Mendeleev's table.
 
• Moseley's work led to the modern formulation of the **Periodic Law**.
 
 
 
• **Lothar Meyer**__
 __
 
• **Lothar Meyer**, a German chemist, independently developed a periodic table around the same time as Mendeleev.
 
• While Meyer’s table was similar, it did not receive as much recognition because Mendeleev's table was published first and included **predictions of unknown elements**.
 
 
 
• **Johann Wolfgang Döbereiner**__
 
 
• **Döbereiner** was a German chemist known for his work on **triads**, groups of three elements with similar properties.
 
• His work was an early attempt to group elements and laid the groundwork for future developments in the periodic table.

questions.question: Article 165 of the Constitution of India deals with the appointment of which of the following?

options.text: Chief Justice of the High Court

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Advocate General of the State**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 165** of the **Constitution of India** pertains to the appointment of the **Advocate General of the State**.
 
• The **Advocate General** is the **highest legal officer** in the state and serves as the **chief legal advisor** to the state government.
 
• He/she is appointed by the **Governor of the state** and must be qualified to be appointed as a judge of a **High Court**.
 
• The Advocate General has the right to speak and participate in the proceedings of both the **state legislature's houses**, but cannot vote.
 
• The Advocate General's primary duties include **advising the state government on legal matters**, appearing on behalf of the state in legal cases, and performing other legal duties assigned by the **Governor.**
 
• The position is similar to that of the **Attorney General of India**, who is the legal advisor to the Central Government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chief Justice of the High Court**__

 __
 
• The **Chief Justice of the High Court** is appointed by the **President of India** in consultation with the **Chief Justice of India** and the **Governor of the state**.
 
• This appointment is governed by **Article 217** of the Constitution of India.
 
 
 
• **Chief Minister**__
 __
 
• The **Chief Minister** is the head of the **state government** and is appointed by the **Governor** of the state.
 
• The Chief Minister is usually the leader of the majority party in the state legislature.
 
 
 
• **Judges of the High Court**__
 
 
• Judges of the High Court are appointed by the **President of India** under **Article 217**, in consultation with the **Chief Justice of India**, the **Governor of the state**, and the Chief Justice of the High Court.
 
• They are responsible for upholding the **rule of law** and interpreting the Constitution at the state level.

questions.question: During the 1930s, Lord Zetland played a significant role in which of the following events related to India's constitutional reforms?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Round Table Conferences**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• During the **1930s**, India witnessed significant discussions about its **constitutional reforms**, and the **Round Table Conferences** were central to these discussions.
 
• The **Round Table Conferences** were a series of meetings held between **1930 and 1932**, organized by the **British Government** to discuss constitutional reforms in India.
 
• **Lord Zetland**, as the **Secretary of State for India** during this period, played a critical role in these conferences.
 
• The conferences were held in **London** and aimed to negotiate the future governance structure of India.
 
• The **First Round Table Conference** was held in **November 1930**, the **Second Round Table Conference** in **September 1931**, and the **Third Round Table Conference** in **November 1932**.
 
• The key participants included representatives of the **Indian National Congress, princely states, minority communities, and British officials**.
 
• The conferences led to the eventual formulation of the **Government of India Act, 1935**, which introduced significant administrative changes.
 
• **Lord Zetland's involvement** was crucial in mediating discussions and ensuring British interests were upheld during the debates.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Simon Commission**__

 __
 
• The **Simon Commission** was a group of British Parliament members sent to India in **1927** to study constitutional reforms.
 
• It faced strong opposition in India because it did not include any **Indian members**.
 
• The **Lahore Congress** of 1929, led by **Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru**, declared complete independence as the goal in opposition to the Simon Commission.
 
 
 
• **Cabinet Mission Plan**__
 __
 
• The **Cabinet Mission Plan** was sent to India in **1946** to discuss the transfer of power from British rule to Indian leadership.
 
• It proposed the formation of a **Constituent Assembly** and a **three-tier federal structure**.
 
• The plan was significant in laying the foundation for India's **independence and constitution drafting**.
 
 
 
• **Quit India Movement**__
 
 
• The **Quit India Movement** was launched by the **Indian National Congress** under the leadership of **Mahatma Gandhi** in **August 1942**.
 
• It was a mass civil disobedience campaign demanding an end to British rule in India.
 
• The movement faced severe repression, including arrests of prominent leaders and violent suppression by the British authorities.

questions.question: What is the eligibility criteria of annual income for EWS households’ families under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Urban (PMAY-U) 2.0?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**up to ₹3 lakh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Economically Weaker Section (EWS)** is a category defined under the **Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Urban (PMAY-U)** to ensure housing benefits for families with limited income.
 
• The eligibility criteria for EWS households under PMAY-U 2.0 specifies that the annual income of the family should be **up to ₹3 lakh.**
 
• Families falling under the EWS category are prioritized for affordable housing schemes designed by the government.
 
• PMAY-U is a flagship mission launched by the **Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA)** to provide housing for all urban families by the year **2022**.
 
• Under PMAY-U, beneficiaries from EWS families can avail subsidies on housing loans through the **Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme (CLSS).**
 
• This scheme aims to improve the **living conditions** of urban poor families by providing pucca houses with basic amenities.
 
• The mission also aligns with the government’s larger goal of ensuring **inclusive growth** by addressing urban housing shortages.
 
• EWS families are identified based on their **income criteria** and are eligible for government assistance in constructing or purchasing houses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **₹6 lakh up to ₹9 lakh**__

 __
 
• This income range falls under the **Middle Income Group-I (MIG-I)** category as defined in PMAY-U.
 
• MIG-I households are eligible for subsidies on housing loans under the **Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme (CLSS).**
 
• Families in this category have access to housing benefits, but they do not qualify as EWS households.
 
 
 
• **up to ₹6 lakh**__
 __
 
• This option corresponds to the eligibility criteria for the **Low Income Group (LIG)** category under PMAY-U.
 
• Families in this income group are eligible for housing benefits under the scheme but are distinct from the EWS category.
 
 
 
• **₹7 lakh up to ₹9 lakh**__
 
 
• Similar to ₹6 lakh up to ₹9 lakh, this option belongs to the **MIG-I category** as defined under PMAY-U.
 
• It does not represent the eligibility criteria for EWS households.

questions.question: Which of the following is a benefit of e-commerce?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Wider market reach**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **E-commerce** provides businesses the ability to expand their market beyond geographical boundaries.
 
• It enables businesses to connect with customers across various **countries and regions**, irrespective of their physical location.
 
• With the use of **digital platforms**, businesses can sell products and services to a larger audience without the need for physical stores.
 
• E-commerce platforms such as **Amazon, Alibaba, and Flipkart** serve as excellent examples of how businesses can reach a global market.
 
• It allows businesses to cater to **niche markets** that might not be accessible through traditional retail methods.
 
• The widespread use of **internet and mobile devices** has played a significant role in ensuring that e-commerce businesses can reach their target customers effectively.
 
• E-commerce also provides opportunities for **24/7 operations**, ensuring customers can shop at their convenience, further enhancing market reach.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Limited choice of products**__

 __
 
• E-commerce platforms generally offer a **wide variety of products**, making the term "limited choice" incorrect in this context.
 
• The digital nature of e-commerce allows businesses to list extensive product catalogs that would not be feasible in a physical store.
 
 
 
• **Higher operating costs**__
 __
 
• E-commerce usually has **lower operating costs** compared to traditional retail stores due to reduced overhead expenses like rent and utilities.
 
• Costs such as logistics and website maintenance are generally lower than maintaining multiple physical stores.
 
 
 
• **Reduced customer services**__
 
 
• E-commerce often enhances customer service by providing **features like live chat, FAQs, and automated systems** to address customer concerns.
 
• Many platforms also offer **personalized recommendations** and 24/7 support, which improve customer experience.
